    The graph of y=−3x2+5x−1y = -3x^2 + 5x - 1y=−3x2+5x−1 is a parabola. How does it open, and how does its width compare with the graph of y=x2y = x^2y=x2?

    Answer choices for question 1

    Solution

    Correct answer: C

    You chose A: Reads the direction correctly but reverses the width rule, treating ∣a∣=3>1|a| = 3 > 1∣a∣=3>1 as wider instead of narrower.

    You chose B: Reads the width correctly but takes the direction from the positive linear coefficient b=5b = 5b=5, missing that only a=−3<0a = -3 < 0a=−3<0 decides it.

    You chose D: Ignores both the sign and the size of aaa, defaulting to an upward, wide parabola.

    Both readings come from the leading coefficient a=−3a = -3a=−3 alone. Its sign is negative, so the parabola opens downward; its size ∣a∣=3|a| = 3∣a∣=3 exceeds the 111 in y=x2y = x^2y=x2, so the parabola is narrower.

    a=−3<0  ⇒  opens downward,∣a∣=3>1  ⇒  narrower.a = -3 < 0 \;\Rightarrow\; \text{opens downward}, \qquad |a| = 3 > 1 \;\Rightarrow\; \text{narrower}.a=−3<0⇒opens downward,∣a∣=3>1⇒narrower.

    Which is the standard equation of the circle with center (4,−2)(4, -2)(4,−2) and radius 555?

    Answer choices for question 2

    Solution

    Correct answer: A

    You chose B: Copies the center's yyy-coordinate straight in as y−2y - 2y−2, instead of subtracting the negative to get y+2y + 2y+2.

    You chose C: Puts the radius itself on the right side rather than its square r2=25r^2 = 25r2=25.

    You chose D: Reverses the sign of each center coordinate, as if the standard form added the center rather than subtracting it.

    Standard form is (x−h)2+(y−k)2=r2(x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2(x−h)2+(y−k)2=r2 with center (h,k)(h, k)(h,k). Here h=4h = 4h=4, k=−2k = -2k=−2, and r=5r = 5r=5, and y−(−2)y - (-2)y−(−2) becomes y+2y + 2y+2.

    (x−4)2+(y+2)2=52=25.(x - 4)^2 + (y + 2)^2 = 5^2 = 25.(x−4)2+(y+2)2=52=25.

    y=−2(x−(−3))2+7  ⇒  (h,k)=(−3,7).y = -2\bigl(x - (-3)\bigr)^2 + 7 \;\Rightarrow\; (h, k) = (-3, 7).y=−2(x−(−3))2+7⇒(h,k)=(−3,7).

    How many times does the graph of y=x2+4x+9y = x^2 + 4x + 9y=x2+4x+9 cross the xxx-axis?

    Answer choices for question 7

    Solution

    Correct answer: B

    You chose A: Assumes every parabola meets the xxx-axis twice, without checking the discriminant.

    You chose C: Treats the negative discriminant as the repeated-root case, which actually needs b2−4ac=0b^2 - 4ac = 0b2−4ac=0.

    You chose D: Believes the crossing count is only visible on a graph, though the discriminant settles it algebraically.

    The number of xxx-intercepts is the number of real roots, which the discriminant counts.

    b2−4ac=(4)2−4(1)(9)=16−36=−20<0.b^2 - 4ac = (4)^2 - 4(1)(9) = 16 - 36 = -20 < 0.b2−4ac=(4)2−4(1)(9)=16−36=−20<0.

    A negative discriminant means no real roots, so the parabola never crosses the xxx-axis.

    The circle (x−1)2+(y−2)2=169(x - 1)^2 + (y - 2)^2 = 169(x−1)2+(y−2)2=169 is given. Where does the point (6,14)(6, 14)(6,14) lie relative to it?

    Answer choices for question 9

    Solution

    Correct answer: C

    You chose A: Computes the distance as 131313, then compares it with r2=169r^2 = 169r2=169, reading 13<16913 < 16913<169 as inside.

    You chose B: Adds the coordinate gaps 5+12=175 + 12 = 175+12=17 and compares with the radius 131313, reading 17>1317 > 1317>13 as outside.

    You chose D: Believes a point's position needs a drawn graph, though comparing distance with the radius settles it.

    Compare the distance from the center (1,2)(1, 2)(1,2) to the point against the radius r=169=13r = \sqrt{169} = 13r=169​=13.

    d=(6−1)2+(14−2)2=25+144=169=13.d = \sqrt{(6 - 1)^2 + (14 - 2)^2} = \sqrt{25 + 144} = \sqrt{169} = 13.d=(6−1)2+(14−2)2​=25+144​=169​=13.

    The distance equals the radius exactly, so the point lies on the circle.

    1. What a parabola tells you before you plot it . 8 points. Question 1 of 10.

    8 pts

    The quadratic y=2x2−8x+3y = 2x^2 - 8x + 3y=2x2−8x+3 is written in standard form. Several features of its graph can be read straight from the three coefficients, with no plotting and no solving.

    1. A
      Part A.

    One honest counterexample breaks a claim about EVERY parabola. Take y=x2+2x+5y = x^2 + 2x + 5y=x2+2x+5.

    b2−4ac=(2)2−4(1)(5)=4−20=−16<0.b^2 - 4ac = (2)^2 - 4(1)(5) = 4 - 20 = -16 < 0.b2−4ac=(2)2−4(1)(5)=4−20=−16<0.

    A negative discriminant means no real roots, so this parabola has zero xxx-intercepts, not two.

    Part B

    Compute the discriminant with a=1a = 1a=1, b=−6b = -6b=−6, c=9c = 9c=9.

    (−6)2−4(1)(9)=36−36=0.(-6)^2 - 4(1)(9) = 36 - 36 = 0.(−6)2−4(1)(9)=36−36=0.

    A zero discriminant means exactly one real root, which happens geometrically when the vertex rests on the xxx-axis rather than above or below it.

    Part C

    The roots come from the quadratic formula,

    x=−b±D2a,x = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{D}}{2a},x=2a−b±D​​,

    so a positive DDD gives two real roots, D=0D = 0D=0 gives one, and D<0D < 0D<0 gives none.

    Restricting to a>0a > 0a>0 does not help: the sign of DDD is decided by aaa, bbb, and ccc together, and opening upward forces none of them. The part A quadratic has a=1>0a = 1 > 0a=1>0 yet D=−16<0D = -16 < 0D=−16<0, so an upward parabola with no crossings already exists.

    In one line

    The claim fails: y=x2+2x+5y = x^2 + 2x + 5y=x2+2x+5 has D=−16<0D = -16 < 0D=−16<0 and no xxx-intercepts, while y=x2−6x+9y = x^2 - 6x + 9y=x2−6x+9 has D=0D = 0D=0 and exactly one, its vertex on the axis. In general D>0D > 0D>0 gives two, D=0D = 0D=0 gives one, and D<0D < 0D<0 gives none, and the sign of aaa alone never forces D>0D > 0D>0.

      Part A.

      An upward-opening quadratic stays above the axis for every real xxx exactly when it has no real roots. Write the discriminant of x2−6x+kx^2 - 6x + kx2−6x+k in terms of kkk, and the condition on it that forces no real roots.

    Part A

    b2−4ac=36−4kb^2 - 4ac = 36 - 4kb2−4ac=36−4k; no real roots requires 36−4k<036 - 4k < 036−4k<0.

    Part B

    k>9k > 9k>9.

    At k=9k = 9k=9 the quadratic is x2−6x+9=(x−3)2x^2 - 6x + 9 = (x - 3)^2x2−6x+9=(x−3)2, which equals 000 at x=3x = 3x=3 instead of staying strictly positive there. So k=9k = 9k=9 fails the strict requirement, which is why the answer is k>9k > 9k>9, not k≥9k \ge 9k≥9.

    x2−6x+9=(x−3)2.x^2 - 6x + 9 = (x - 3)^2.x2−6x+9=(x−3)2.

    11 pts

    A ball is thrown straight up; its height in feet after ttt seconds is h=−16t2+48t+40h = -16t^2 + 48t + 40h=−16t2+48t+40.

      Part A.

      Part C.

      Compare the two methods Say what each one costs you, and when you would reach for it. 4 points

    The answer

    Part A

    The peak is at t=1.5t = 1.5t=1.5 seconds (the optimizing input), and the peak height is 767676 feet (the optimal value).

    Part B

    No. Setting h=80h = 80h=80 gives 2t2−6t+5=02t^2 - 6t + 5 = 02t2−6t+5=0, whose discriminant is 36−40=−4<036 - 40 = -4 < 036−40=−4<0, so no real time reaches 808080 feet.

    Part C

    The peak height 767676 feet is the highest the ball reaches, so 808080 feet is impossible, exactly what the negative discriminant shows. The peak time used only aaa and bbb; the peak height also used ccc, the launch height, which is what put 808080 out of reach.

    Worked solution

    Part A

    The peak time comes from −b2a-\tfrac{b}{2a}−2ab​, and the peak height from substituting it back.

    t=−482(−16)=1.5,h=−16(1.5)2+48(1.5)+40=−36+72+40=76.t = -\frac{48}{2(-16)} = 1.5, \qquad h = -16(1.5)^2 + 48(1.5) + 40 = -36 + 72 + 40 = 76.t=−2(−16)48​=1.5,h=−16(1.5)2+48(1.5)+40=−36+72+40=76.

    Part B

    Set the height equal to 808080 and gather to one side.

    −16t2+48t+40=80  ⇒  2t2−6t+5=0.-16t^2 + 48t + 40 = 80 \;\Rightarrow\; 2t^2 - 6t + 5 = 0.−16t2+48t+40=80⇒2t2−6t+5=0.

    The discriminant is (−6)2−4(2)(5)=36−40=−4<0(-6)^2 - 4(2)(5) = 36 - 40 = -4 < 0(−6)2−4(2)(5)=36−40=−4<0, so there is no real solution: the ball never reaches 808080 feet.

    Part C

    The peak height is the greatest value hhh ever takes, so a target above it can never be met.

    76<80  ⇒  no real time gives a height of 80 feet,76 < 80 \;\Rightarrow\; \text{no real time gives a height of } 80 \text{ feet},76<80⇒no real time gives a height of 80 feet,

    which is exactly why part B's discriminant came out negative.

    The peak time came from −b2a-\tfrac{b}{2a}−2ab​, using only aaa and bbb. The peak height came from substituting that time back, which brings in ccc as well. So ccc, the launch height, is the coefficient that decides how high the peak is, and therefore whether 808080 feet is reachable.

    In one line

    The ball peaks at t=1.5t = 1.5t=1.5 seconds (the input) at a height of 767676 feet (the value). It never reaches 808080 feet: h=80h = 80h=80 gives 2t2−6t+5=02t^2 - 6t + 5 = 02t2−6t+5=0 with discriminant −4<0-4 < 0−4<0. Since the peak height 767676 is already below 808080, the negative discriminant is no surprise, and the peak height additionally depends on ccc, the launch height, while the peak time uses only aaa and bbb.
